analyzed_vuln.description: The FIELD_DD macro expanded inside dwg_decode_MINSERT_private performs TRACE_DD before calling the bounds-checked bit_read_DD. TRACE_DD unconditionally initializes `byte` with `dat->chain[dat->byte]` without first checking `dat->byte < dat->size`. When the MINSERT object bit-chain is exhausted, this diagnostic read goes past the heap allocation; bit_read_DD never gets a chance to apply its own overflow checks. The patch-relevant defect is the unchecked TRACE_DD read in dec_macros.h, expanded at dwg.spec:840.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: A fuzz-supplied AC1015/R2000 DWG is decoded through the object map as a MINSERT object. Its fields select `scale_flag == 0`, so dwg_decode_MINSERT_private reads scale.x and then invokes `FIELD_DD(scale.y, scale.x, 42)`. The declared/truncated object data leaves the restricted Bit_Chain exhausted at that point (`dat->byte == dat->size`, observed as 0 == 0), and TRACE_DD directly reads `dat->chain[dat->byte]`, producing the one-byte heap-buffer-overflow. Any similarly truncated MINSERT reaching a FIELD_DD at the exact object boundary can trigger this path.

The reported ASan crash occurs in dwg_decode_MINSERT_private at dwg.spec:840 through FIELD_DD(scale.y,...). FIELD_DD expands TRACE_DD before bit_read_DD. TRACE_DD currently initializes BITCODE_RC byte = dat->chain[dat->byte] unconditionally and later tests dat->byte < dat->size - 1. For a restricted exhausted chain, byte == size == 0, so the initial diagnostic read is out of bounds and the subtraction may also underflow. bit_read_DD itself has bounds checking. I am considering guarding the entire diagnostic decode with dat->chain && dat->byte < dat->size, defaulting the trace result to zero when exhausted, and replacing the lookahead condition with dat->byte + 1 < dat->size or a subtraction-safe equivalent.
